title: Reading Execution Plans
description: Interpret EXPLAIN output to find slow scans, missing indexes, and bad joins

data.text: Execution plans show how the database executes a query. Reading them reveals full table scans, missing indexes, expensive sorts, and join strategy choices.

data.title: Watch for
items: Nested Loop with high row estimates
Hash Join with unexpected hash matches

data.title: EXPLAIN ANALYZE output
data.content: Analyze a slow query and identify the bottleneck.
data.code:
EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT o.order_id, c.name, o.total
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
WHERE o.created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '30 days'
  AND c.country = 'US'
ORDER BY o.total DESC
LIMIT 100;

data.title: Important
data.text: Always run EXPLAIN ANALYZE, not just EXPLAIN. Actual timing and row counts reveal discrepancies between estimates and reality.

items.question: What is the most common red flag?
items.answer: Seq Scan on a table with millions of rows where an index could help.

items.question: Why does the plan change with parameters?
items.answer: The optimizer uses parameter sniffing or generic plans. Test with actual parameter values.

items.question: Should I always avoid Seq Scan?
items.answer: No. For small tables or returning most rows, Seq Scan can be faster than index lookups.

data.title: Summary
points: Start with EXPLAIN ANALYZE for timing
Identify Seq Scans and high-cost nodes
data.takeaway: Execution plans are the primary debugging tool for query performance. Learn the node types and cost indicators for your database.
